question.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{y}+z$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨4,\operatorname{ln}⁡t,{e}^{t}⟩$ at the point $t=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}+z),\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}+z),\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{e}^{y}+z)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y},x{e}^{y},1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=4,$ $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡t$ and $z={e}^{t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡t},4{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡t},1⟩ \\  & =⟨t,4t,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\frac{1}{t},{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨t,4t,1⟩\cdot ⟨0,\frac{1}{t},{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =t\cdot 0+4t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+1\cdot {e}^{t} \\  & =4+{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(2))] & =4+{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
